agent_priors_used: GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): when multiple independent agent lanes fail within minutes with the identical error signature (same model id, same exit code, same fingerprint, same control revision), the shared component, not the lanes' science, is the cause; repair the component once at the control plane instead of re-deriving new directions from the failures.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): a retryable execution failure (exit 75) that carries no output is an operational event, not evidence; a frozen experiment must be allowed to complete before any redirection is considered.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): prompt specification and model capability are separate failure modes; a 0/N result under an underspecified prompt cannot be attributed to capability until the specification variable is directly tested.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): a benchmark whose baselines sit at the ceiling has zero dynamic range and cannot detect a treatment effect even if the treatment is good - ceiling baselines are a null instrument, not weak evidence.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): continuing a mature thread is correct when the next result can still change an important architecture or product decision; and pre-freeze design-satisfiability failures (unsatisfiable gates, empty sampling frames, absent certificates) should be fixed once through the design-contract protocol rather than re-purchased cycle after cycle.

GENERAL PRIOR (not SPIDER evidence): long-lived research agents over-exploit their deepest local thread; a Global Director should prefer removing one shared blocker once over letting each lane re-discover the same absence.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: LEGACY: DISTINCT_EXTENSION. P2-BLIND-COMPOSITION (pre2 artifact 4.697, sha 017a80aeb9a6759c8f6913a37031ff1616ec1bda) reported 3/3 unseen compositions vs 0/3 weak baselines but only with keyword/oracle dependence - the same confound class (joint authorship / oracle assistance) this experiment removes; P2-MIND2WEB (archived Codex section 1) found retrieval 47/176 vs exact human routes 6/176, supporting retrieve-and-bind over exact-route replay and consistent with an embedding-selection mechanism. This experiment materially improves on both by independently authoring goals, screening contamination against every registry intent, and proving the reference arm distinct from the candidate. Not a pointless rerun: the bounded 45/52 vs 33/52 Research 2.0 result was never tested without the joint-authorship confound, and the design-contract v2 controls make the accept and reject regions arithmetically reachable. Search limitation: legacy index is topic/path keyed; only the named pins were inspected.
allocation.question: On a stdlib-only locally served multi-endpoint multi-verb HTTP application whose goal texts are authored by a process that never sees the mechanism intent strings, with a preregistered contamination screen measuring every goal's overlap against EVERY intent in the registry, a preregistered authoring-provenance record, a reference arm provably distinct from the candidate, and positive/null/dynamic-range controls that are each arithmetically able to fail and are live-verified before freeze: does max-cosine-similarity selection over intent embeddings still bind the correct mechanism on goals never seen at authoring time, and by how much does it exceed a token-overlap null on those same independently authored goals - i.e., does the bounded 45/52 versus 33/52 advantage (paired family-blocked difference 0.2308, 95% CI [0.1136,0.3509]) survive removal of the joint-authorship confound, or was it an artifact of intents and goal templates being authored in the same execute-time file by the same agent that reported the numbers?

The mild, explicit tension with the audit's 'keep Graph on freshness/safety' guidance is accepted because no ready non-four-anchor freshness test exists while this clean capability test is ready. C-FRESHNESS remains EXPERIMENTAL and the parked D1V route stays parked. The active experiment EXP-GRAPH-38109260004 passed model_design but was blocked by the shared design-review model routing failure; it must be re-dispatched under the same mandate.
